key_insight: Recurrent quantum reinforcement learning improves Hamiltonian tracking when quantum-system dynamics change over time.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive Hamiltonian estimation could support quantum-device calibration and monitoring under parameter drift or changing operating conditions.
method: Formulate Hamiltonian identification as QRL using sequential quantum-state observations.
Use Vanilla-QRL for stationary dynamics and recurrent GRU-QRL for time-varying dynamics.
Compare against a Quantum Graph Recurrent Neural Network baseline and test frozen policies on unseen trajectories.
evidence_signal: Evaluations on transverse-field Ising systems cover stationary dynamics, abrupt and rapid switching, randomized switch locations, and gradual drift, with substantially improved non-stationary tracking reported for GRU-QRL.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish robustness to hardware noise, measurement costs, or scaling beyond the evaluated Ising systems.
paper_title: Adaptive Hamiltonian Identification via Quantum Reinforcement Learning under Non-Stationary Dynamics
